$comment: What the factory reads to run mold_v0 (.claude/scripts/lib/single_service.py). The codebase next to it is AUTHORED IN THIS REPOSITORY since the fork point below (operator decision D1, 2026-10-20; mold_v0-040), a recorded exception to 'never edit a mold in place' (MOLD.md). Every product-specific value the factory needs (env names, the service, its port) is still READ from the codebase's own files at plan time, so this file names paths and rules only.

source.$comment: in_tree: the codebase is edited here and never fetched, refreshed or rewritten by mold.py (lib/intree.py). since: the factory commit whose snapshot is the fork point. forked_from: the source commit that snapshot was taken at (the operator's product with mold_v0-031's hardening merged); nothing is ever fetched from it again. ci.workflow: the factory workflow whose run the deploy gate requires for the commit being deployed (lib/deploy_gate.py). null until mold_v0-001 adds it: until then the gate requires at least one GitHub Actions check of this repository to have succeeded for that commit and nothing (from any app) to have failed or be running.

env_names.$comment: The shell's environment names (mold_v0-045; MOLD.md "Neutral words and environment names"): every name it reads starts with `prefix`; until mold_v0-045 they started with `legacy_prefix`, which it still reads as a fallback. The factory (lib/single_service.py env_aliases) takes a name held under either spelling as present (a value under the old name is never minted again under the new one, which would win over it), mints a state name in the old spelling from the bootstrap's new one, accepts --set-secret on an app's old names, and on a server copies each old name's value to its new name in the env file before anything is minted. New apps get the new names from the codebase as before.

rls.$comment: The product's own row-level security proof (mold_v0-031; its scripts/check-rls.ts: the catalog, then a live probe in a rolled-back transaction). Applies only while the codebase's package.json has the script. Intake writes datastores.postgres.rls = mode; the deploy runs the script (compose_remote: in a one-off container of the new release, with the server's env file; vercel: on this machine against the api project's production database) and a failure is a failed health check; the lanes run it against an embedded throwaway database. A deploy counts only the product's PASS line for a real Postgres ('pass'), never one for its embedded fallback.

console.$comment: The web console on a server of its own (mold_v0-020): the compose service built from web/Dockerfile (Next.js standalone output) behind the stack's Caddy, which sends the API's own paths to the API service and everything else to the console. Health: the API's health path answers 200 ok THROUGH the console (so its API-address variable reaches the API), and these pages answer without following a redirect (a page, its sign-in redirect, or 401/403; never a 5xx or nothing). operator_env: the names in the server's env file the console needs from the operator (its sign-in; the API reads the same two), asked for at a hidden prompt during the deploy when the server lacks them. Optional since mold_v0-004: without them the console and the API run the built-in sign-in (an emailed code, and Google when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are set); an app whose state lists them keeps Clerk.

vercel.$comment: TWO projects on Vercel (operator's decision 2026-10-20, ticket mold_v0-029): <project>-api is the API and MCP function from the root vercel.json, the only one with the app's own Neon Postgres and the product's minted keys; <project> is the web console (web/, a server-rendered Next.js app behind a middleware) as its own Next.js project, given the API's address through the one variable its next.config reads (found there at plan time, never named here) and only the sign-in names below: optional since mold_v0-004, as the console signs people in with the built-in emailed code (and Google) unless Clerk's keys are set; an app whose state already lists them in secrets_user keeps Clerk, and AUTH_PROVIDER (builtin or clerk) overrides the rule. Deployed api first; both rolled back if either fails its health.

env.$comment: Settings the factory writes on the api project at every deploy (mold_v0-084), never secrets: {console_url} is the console project's production address, read back from Vercel after its deploy (the API is deployed once more when it changed), so sign-in codes, invitations and every email link to the console; APP_PROXY_HOPS is the one proxy in front of the function (Vercel's edge), so per-IP limits read the address the edge saw; {platform_admins} is the app's platform administrators (application.json platform_admins, comma-separated addresses or *@domain entries; src/clerk.ts), the only people besides a company account's members who may sign in and reach /admin. While state records none, the name is not written and whatever the project holds under either spelling (env_names) is kept (provision.py's check says so; with neither, the check and the deploy stop and ask). A project that holds the old spelling gets the same value under both.

packs.$comment: Where an app's packs go and what proves the mold takes them (.claude/scripts/packs.py; mold_v0-024; MOLD.md "Pack and record-area contract"). A factory pack packs/<id>/files/ mirrors the codebase root and may add files ONLY under packs/<its own id>/ ({pack} is substituted with the pack's id, so it cannot write into another pack or the shell): its pack.json, its definePack entry, its migrations, its run programs. Its console pages need no files of their own: they render through the shell's generic page (web/src/app/{app,admin}/packs/[pack]/[page]) from pack.json. A file that already exists in the codebase is refused (a pack only adds). The id pattern is the shell's own (scripts/gen-packs.mjs: it is also the pack's table prefix). After copying, the shell's generator writes the registry the server and the console import; gen-packs refuses a pack whose code or SQL gets past the seam. `prune`: a pack folder an earlier apply left in the build copy for a pack the app no longer names is removed, so the registry never lists it. Host packs (mold_v0-039; src/host.ts): a pack named in `host_packs` that the app names is written into the build's profile.json `host_packs`, so it may carry the product's own surface: a host entry, operator scripts, console pages under web/src/packs/{pack}/ and an orchestrator extension under orchestrator/packs/{pack}/, each held to its own import rules by gen-packs. Every other pack is an ordinary one. The generators also write what depends on the packs' surface (mold_v0-039): the console's tool list (scripts/export-mcp-tools.ts), the docs answers' corpus (scripts/sync-docs-corpus.ts) and the internal docs (web/scripts/sync-docs.mjs, which reads a host pack's docs/); `verify` checks each is current. The deploy copy also gets the deploy facts (`deploy_facts`, mold_v0-050): the factory writes deploy-facts.json at its root from the app's state (names, places and providers; never a value) and the operator's source offer into its profile.json before the generators run; gen-packs checks and copies them, and scripts/data-map.ts writes DATA-MAP.md (the data-flow and residency statement), which `verify` checks is current.

build_copy.$comment: How build/<app_id>/ is made from the codebase (.claude/scripts/branding.py build_copy) for an app with packs or a brand: the source tree without these paths (the same the server deploy leaves out), and each node_modules folder the codebase has installed hard-linked in (never written), so the generators and the lanes' npm checks run in the copy. A folder that is not installed is left out; the image and the Vercel builds install their own.

not_needed.workspaces: mold_v0 has organisations of its own, made in its admin console or by its org:create script, not workspaces written from state
not_needed.package: the agent package is mold_v1's (an npm CLI for its chat); mold_v0 is reached from MCP clients through its connector URL
